```{=html}
<section class="hero-shell" aria-labelledby="home-title">
  <div class="hero-grid">
    <div class="hero-copy">
      <p class="eyebrow">Simon Fraser University · School of Resource and Environmental Management</p>
      <h1 id="home-title">Cities <span>&</span> Climate<br>Learning Lab</h1>
      <p class="hero-proposition">How cities find, generate and use evidence for climate action.</p>
      <p class="hero-subtitle">Cities cannot investigate every climate problem independently, but evidence produced in one place cannot be assumed to apply unchanged elsewhere. The Cities and Climate Learning Lab studies how urban climate knowledge is compared across places, where new evidence would matter, how action is organised, and what it changes for people and places.</p>
      <div class="hero-actions">
        <a class="button button-primary" href="research.html">Explore our research</a>

      </div>
    </div>
    <aside class="hero-aside" aria-label="Research programme">
      <p class="index-number">01—04</p>
      <p>Four connected questions about knowledge across places, strategic evidence generation, institutional delivery, and consequences.</p>
      <p class="small-note">Consequences generate new evidence and further learning.</p>
    </aside>
  </div>
</section>
```

```{=html}
<section class="section-shell intro-band" aria-labelledby="problem-heading">
  <p class="eyebrow">The urban climate learning problem</p>
  <div class="split-heading">
    <h2 id="problem-heading">Useful knowledge must be compared, produced, organised and reconsidered.</h2>
    <p>Context shapes whether existing evidence is relevant. Choices about new evidence shape what cities can know. Institutions shape what becomes operable. Consequences reveal benefits, burdens and questions that change later decisions.</p>
  </div>
</section>
```

```{=html}
<section class="section-shell" aria-labelledby="themes-heading">
  <div class="section-header">
    <div><p class="eyebrow">Research programme</p><h2 id="themes-heading">Four connected questions</h2></div>
    <a class="text-link" href="research.html">See the full programme <span aria-hidden="true">→</span></a>
  </div>
  <p class="learning-cycle-intro">Urban climate learning is not a one-way path from evidence to action. The consequences of climate action generate new evidence, expose unresolved questions and change what other places can plausibly learn.</p>
```
